column1: # Known deviations of the implementations under test, verified by hand.
# A failing result matching client, peer and scenario (fnmatch patterns) is
# reported as "known-difference" with the waiver id and the note; it still
# appears in every report. A waiver whose scenario ran and passed no longer
# reproduces, and fails the run: remove the line when the deviation is fixed.

column8: KNXUltimate 6.3.1 announces <local IP>:3671 in its DESCRIPTION_REQUEST HPAI while it listens on an ephemeral port (src/KNXClient.ts sendDescriptionRequestMessage: new HPAI(localIPAddress), default port 3671); servers that answer to the HPAI, as the standard requires, answer a port nobody listens on. Reported: https://github.com/Supergiovane/KNXUltimate/issues/117

calimero-server 3.0-M1 stops answering for about 10 s after a 3-octet datagram: its log shows the control endpoint coming up again ("control endpoint ... is up and running"); cause: an uncaught KNXIllegalArgumentException ("negative length of message body") in UdpServiceLooper closes the control endpoint; fixed upstream after 3.0-M2 by calimero-server d276d8a8 (2026-09-14), not in a release or image yet
calimero-server 3.0-M1 stops answering for about 10 s after a CONNECT_REQUEST whose CRI has length 0, the same uncaught exception as after a truncated header; fixed upstream by d276d8a8

column4: Data Secure group write through a secure tunnel*
column8: calimero-tools 3.0-M1 send Data Secure group telegrams only through a surrogate device (S-A_Sync and group object diagnostics with the surrogate's tool key) and require every sender of the group in the keyring to be such a device; the profile's tunnel groups list the tunnel addresses as senders, and no surrogate is on the tunnel. Through secure routing, with go-knx as the surrogate, it works (secure routing scenarios).

column4: Data Secure group write over secure routing*
column8: calimero-tools 3.0-M1 send Data Secure group telegrams only through a surrogate device; xknx does not act as one, and the pairing has no go-knx on the network. Towards go-knx, the surrogate, it passes.
